context: These equations (\cref{eq:kinematics} and \cref{eq:gl}) state how a chosen mapping is converted into a chosen strain; they say nothing about whether \(\boldsymbol\varphi\) is correct. The conversion itself has consequences for error. Differentiation can amplify local mapping error, while smoothing can reduce variance and alter peaks or spatial gradients. The reported number further depends on coordinate axes, myocardial layer, reference frame, segment definition, spatial aggregation and whether ``peak'' means the minimum of a segment-average curve or the average of pointwise minima. A comparison that ignores these choices can attribute a definitional difference to a tracking error~\cite{voigt2015,wehner2018}.

context: Feature-tracking (FT) software is attractive because it operates on routine cine and fits existing clinical workflows. Initial contours are propagated through the cardiac cycle, after which strain may be calculated from endocardial length, a myocardial mesh or a vendor-specific deformation field; interior motion is to a large degree interpolated from boundary behaviour~\cite{pedrizzetti2016}. Because each of these steps can be implemented differently, the phrase ``feature tracking'' denotes a family of measurements. Commercial implementations have differed in contour placement, transmural treatment, radial-strain calculation, temporal interpolation and user correction. As a consequence, values may fail to be interchangeable across products or software versions even when repeatability within a product is acceptable~\cite{lim2021,militaru2021}.

context: The following examples distinguish the acquisition used at inference, the learning target and the endpoint used for evaluation. They include cine pipelines and methods that analyse the material-sensitive comparator itself. DeepTag estimates motion on tagged images without labels, using bidirectional diffeomorphic registration between consecutive frames and a differentiable composition layer to recover the Lagrangian field, validated by landmark tracking on a clinical tagging dataset~\cite{ye2021deeptag}. Networks trained on synthetic 3D tagged images from a biophysical left-ventricular model have since been evaluated for 3D tagging analysis, including an external human landmark comparison and porcine strain comparisons with manual cine annotations~\cite{buoso2025tagging3d}; like DeepTag, they operate on the comparator acquisition and not on cine. DeepStrain provides an end-to-end cine workflow. It centres the ventricle, segments anatomy, estimates end-diastole-to-phase displacement and derives Green--Lagrange radial and circumferential strain, and the original study reported a Cardiac Motion Analysis Challenge (CMAC) landmark end-point error of \(2.9\pm1.5\)~mm together with scan--rescan repeatability in ten healthy volunteers and high agreement for volumetric measures~\cite{morales2021}. A later single-centre comparison in 47 healthy participants and 533 patients found correlations with manual feature-tracking analysis of 0.83--0.85 for global radial and 0.88--0.91 for global circumferential strain~\cite{morales2022comparison}; in that comparison the comparator is another estimator. These results establish workflow and output properties. Independent dense material truth for the cine motion field is a separate matter, and a prescribed-motion evaluation of DeepStrain is discussed in \cref{sec:knownmotion}.

context: StrainNet is particularly relevant because DENSE phase-derived displacement was the supervised target, and its two evaluations must be read separately. Of 305 eligible individuals (161 patients, 99 healthy adults and 45 healthy children or adolescents), 243 individuals contributing 670 sections formed the training set and 62 individuals contributing 190 sections formed the participant-held-out internal test set; the 305 were not independent held-out cine tests. For pixelwise displacement end-point error (EPE), the model was deliberately given contours derived from DENSE magnitude images, permitting one-to-one comparison with DENSE phase-derived displacement over the myocardium and time series; the held-out-test EPE was \(0.75\pm0.35\)~mm. In the distinct routine-cine analysis, contours from bSSFP cine feature tracking were supplied to StrainNet and registered DENSE was the comparator. End-systolic global and AHA-segmental circumferential Green--Lagrange strain was analysed in 59 of the 62 test participants with basal, mid-ventricular and apical images: ICCs were 0.87 versus 0.72 globally and 0.75 versus 0.48 segmentally for StrainNet versus conventional feature tracking~\cite{wang2023strainnet}. The improvement in ICC was accompanied by prose-reported cine--DENSE limits of agreement of \(-5.74\) to 4.72 percentage points globally and \(-9.16\) to 8.07 percentage points segmentally. A small discrepancy between the source prose and table for the global limits is documented in Supplementary Table~S1. The study used an internal participant split, with cine-mask preprocessing and resolution matching; external-dataset validation was not performed. These results support improved end-systolic Ecc agreement, while the remaining individual differences require comparison with an intended-use tolerance. The two tests retain distinct interpretations: the EPE is not a cine-contour result, ``global'' strain is not the pixelwise whole-myocardium EPE, and end-systolic values are not peak-strain timing. The inference therefore remains model-, direction-, population-, acquisition- and registration-specific, and it does not establish focal location or extent.

context: Numerical phantoms make exact correspondence available. A simple realistic phantom showed that spatial and temporal resolution can materially affect feature-tracking measurements~\cite{adams2023}. MRXCAT2.0 couples statistical shape, biophysical simulation and tissue texture to produce healthy and pathological cine-like images paired with known functional ground truth~\cite{mrxcat2023}. Other in-silico heart models and DENSE-SIM extend controlled testing of strain pipelines and acquisition effects~\cite{mukherjee2024,barbaroux2025}. The design that such resources make possible, a graded regional deficit measured against a material reference while the estimator is held fixed, has a precedent outside cine: Yeon and colleagues compared tagged circumferential shortening with implanted sonomicrometry crystals in a canine coronary-ligation model, with both methods separating ischaemic from remote myocardium~\cite{yeon2001sonomicrometry}. This provides a precedent for regional reference-based testing, although it is not a controlled sweep of lesion size or severity in routine cine.

context: MRXCAT2.0 provides a useful prescribed-focal example: an evaluation of DeepStrain by a separate development team. Four left-ventricular cases were generated (normal, dilated, hypertrophic and infarcted; ejection fractions 51\%, 34\%, 41\% and 49\%). An elliptical free-wall scar was prescribed in the infarct case, while remote compensation preserved its ejection fraction. The underlying abnormality differed by component: remote-to-scar peak systolic strain changed from 0.95 to 0.30 radially (Err), from \(-0.18\) to 0.01 circumferentially (Ecc) and from \(-0.18\) to \(-0.17\) longitudinally (Ell). Radial strain was markedly reduced but retained a substantial residual value; circumferential strain approached zero, while longitudinal strain changed little. These are prescribed tissue values; the estimator's errors are reported separately below~\cite{mrxcat2023}.

context: The generated domain also limits interpretation. The evaluation used one scar geometry and a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 30, and myocardial texture was removed during image generation. The inspected source does not identify the evaluated DeepStrain release or weights. The component-specific errors could reflect image formation, wall thinning and partial volume, training data or estimation constraints; the experiment does not isolate these contributions~\cite{mrxcat2023}.

context: Known-motion resources allow investigators to test representation capacity, recovery at a chosen signal-to-noise ratio and sensitivity to sampling or regularisation. Existing work has varied resolution~\cite{adams2023}, varied analysis regularisation~\cite{barbaroux2025}, or represented regional pathology in simulated motion~\cite{mrxcat2023,zhou2018straus}. These are useful precedents for the proposed validation programme. The surviving search records do not establish whether all combinations of graded lesion size, severity, transmurality and fixed-estimator evaluation have already been studied. Here, graded attribute recovery is proposed as a research priority; the proposal does not rest on a claim of field-wide absence. Simulation results remain conditional on the anatomy, mechanics, image formation and pathology represented; paired in-vivo comparisons are needed to assess transfer.

context: The paired literature is mixed in a scientifically useful way. In three healthy volunteers and 41 patients with recent or chronic myocardial infarction, Gao and colleagues reported agreement in peak circumferential strain and similar regional patterns between cine registration and DENSE, while cine radial strain was overestimated~\cite{gao2014cine}. A larger comparison of 77 patients with cardiomyopathy and ten controls found relatively small circumferential differences but wide radial differences across tagging, DENSE and three feature-tracking products~\cite{cao2018}. Wehner and colleagues showed that part of the apparent cine--DENSE discrepancy can arise from comparing different strain definitions, while still finding that regional tracking information cannot be inferred from contours alone~\cite{wehner2018}.

context: The product dependence seen by Cao and colleagues was examined directly at 3~T by Militaru and colleagues, who compared three feature-tracking products with tagging in 61 participants. Global longitudinal and circumferential agreement was high, regional and radial agreement varied more, and scar discrimination differed by vendor~\cite{militaru2021}. This pattern supports global and some regional use under specified products, and it warns against interchangeability and against extrapolating global performance to radial or highly local outputs; it does not justify a blanket rejection of feature tracking. Among the paired studies reviewed here, timing was compared less often than magnitude. In 42 participants, Brandt and colleagues found moderate-to-good agreement for global and segmental circumferential time to peak strain between tagging and feature tracking, alongside significant biases in segmental peak strain~\cite{brandt2024}. This supports a segment-level timing comparison; a focal peak-time error endpoint was not established by the abstract inspected here.

context: A 2026 study makes the importance of the endpoint explicit. Jahromi and colleagues compared one- and two-slice DENSE models with a one-slice cine model in a deforming phantom and 40 healthy volunteers. In the volunteer comparison, the endpoint was slice-wise peak median systolic endocardial circumferential strain at two mid-ventricular levels. The cine versus two-slice DENSE mean difference was \(-2.7\) percentage points. Two one-sided tests supported equivalence within a selected margin of \(\pm3.5\) percentage points, despite a significant difference from zero; those are compatible findings because they test different hypotheses. Prospective specification of the margin and the handling of within-person slice correlation were not established by the inspected report. The radial, longitudinal and epicardial circumferential comparisons differed~\cite{jahromi2026densecine}. Thus the result supports a specific healthy-volunteer, slice-level, endocardial comparison; it says nothing about focal-lesion accuracy or general interchangeability. Selected studies are compared in \cref{tab:evidence}.

context: Radial strain is repeatedly less consistent than circumferential or longitudinal strain~\cite{cao2018,militaru2021}. Three features of the measurement explain much of this. The ventricular wall spans relatively few voxels radially, trabeculation complicates the endocardial boundary, and a small contour displacement can produce a large relative change in thickness. Products may additionally calculate radial output from different entities. These factors make the definition and uncertainty of radial strain unusually important, without making radial function unknowable. Claims should therefore specify whether the result is tensor radial strain, wall thickening, a layer-to-layer distance change or another surrogate.

context: CMAC paired cine SSFP, 3D tagged MRI and 3D ultrasound from a dynamic phantom and 15 healthy volunteers. Its human reference comprised 12 landmarks (four walls at three LV levels) manually tracked by two observers in 3D tagging, with a reported median inter-observer variability of 0.84~mm~\cite{tobongomez2013cmac,cmac2011}. That reference supports correspondence error at those landmarks and times, and it says nothing about dense strain accuracy between them. The MRXCAT family differs again. Original MRXCAT uses the XCAT phantom to generate cine or perfusion CMR with selectable cardiac/respiratory motion, sampling, coils and noise, and the 2014 demonstration was primarily an acquisition/reconstruction simulator~\cite{wissmann2014mrxcat}. MRXCAT2.0 adds statistical LV shape, biophysical healthy/infarct/dilated/hypertrophic function and generated tissue texture, exposing known simulated function for method testing~\cite{mrxcat2023,mrxcat2repo}. Both are generators with exemplar outputs, so neither has a fixed number of independent participants.

context: Common finite-strain measures include the right Cauchy--Green tensor \(\vect C=\vect F^{\mathsf T}\vect F\), Green--Lagrange strain \(\vect E=(\vect C-\vect I)/2\), and logarithmic strain obtained from a stretch tensor. In one dimension, engineering strain \(e=(\ell-\ell_0)/\ell_0\) and Green--Lagrange strain satisfy \(E=e+e^2/2\). Numerically comparing values without converting the definitions can create an apparent method bias~\cite{wehner2018}.

context: DeepStrain and StrainNet illustrate why the target matters. DeepStrain demonstrated a complete automated workflow with segmentation, motion estimation, volumetric agreement, reference ranges and repeatability analyses~\cite{morales2021}. Its cine motion network was not independently validated against dense material displacement for every regional claim. StrainNet used DENSE phase-derived displacement as a supervised target, but it reported two distinct evaluations~\cite{wang2023strainnet}. In the 62-person internal participant-held-out test set, its \(0.75\pm0.35\)-mm pixelwise EPE was obtained with DENSE-magnitude contours supplied to the network and compared with DENSE displacement over myocardium and time. Separately, bSSFP cine feature-tracking contours were used for the end-systolic global and AHA-segmental circumferential-strain comparison in 59 test participants. Thus the EPE and cine-contour ICCs must not be fused into one ``cine displacement'' result; population, contour source, registration, direction, aggregation and time point still bound the claim.

context: Feature-tracking and strain tools change over time. Regulatory clearance may cover a broad software application or specified outputs but does not establish material-motion accuracy for every regional analysis. Product webpages document current availability; they do not document the historical algorithm behind a published result. Studies should therefore record software name, exact version, analysis module, contour convention, manual corrections and any export transformation. Reference intervals and serial thresholds should not be transferred across products without a bridging study~\cite{lim2021,militaru2021,cao2018}.
